sources.finding: Parrish was inactive with a back injury; Morrison was identified as his expected starting replacement.

Morrison played and recorded seven tackles and a pass defensed. Tampa Bay linebacker Josiah Trotter missed time in the second half with a shoulder injury; that is not a documented full-game absence or an authorized impairment percentage.

Sampson went to IR September 15 and McLaughlin was added to the active roster. Kendrick Green was already on IR and Byers had been waived, so they cannot be assumed available Jenkins replacements. Other retained reserves require role/baseline classification.

Smith entered IR September 1, To'oTo'o September 15, and McDonald September 11. Higgins, Dell, Speed and other pregame reserves also require baseline/role reconciliation; the original Collins/Ingram/Clowney queue is incomplete.

The official postgame report places Trent Brown at right tackle opposite Cashius Howell and Ersery at left tackle. This provides actual Week 2 role evidence, rather than an undated depth-chart assumption.

Burrow was cleared to start after full Friday practice. B.J. Hill was inactive with an Achilles issue, an absence omitted from the archived case queue. Stewart activation is not by itself proof of exclusive Hill-role replacement.

Baltimore identifies Bateman as the No. 1 receiver with Flowers unavailable. Lane was also on IR. Moore, Wester and Walker participated; Sarratt did not take a snap. The report supports Bateman's primary role but not unique shares for every simultaneous receiver absence.
Lane went to IR September 16 and Tampa September 19. Earlier retained reserves remain part of final coverage, not automatic zero losses.
Pre-kickoff reserve records include Tyson, Radunz and Bresee, among others; the source-week archived queue alone is not complete Saints availability coverage.
